beats.text: Every single time Cursor or Claude writes code for you, your GPU wastes up to 70% of its compute doing nothing.
beats.visual_focus: A high-fidelity 3D scene of a city street where the visual motion is fluid, but the audio waveform is a flat, dead line.

beats.text: The bottleneck is the compute-heavy bidirectional teacher. It’s like a film director who needs ten minutes to calculate the sound for every single frame.
beats.visual_focus: A massive, glowing neural network node (teacher) struggling to process a single frame, while a clock ticks aggressively in the background.

beats.text: HelixWorld solves this by distilling the teacher into a streaming student, using an online trajectory loss to synchronize audio-visual rollouts at 24 FPS.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—calling out that current models are 'deaf' actually made me stop scrolling because it's a valid pain point. I liked the director analogy in Beat 2; it wasn't patronizing, just a good way to explain the latency issue. I got a bit lost on 'online trajectory loss'—I get the gist that it's keeping the audio and video aligned in real-time, but it sounds like a buzzword if you don't explain how it's actually calculating that error signal.
